item.title: Experiences of stigma among adult learners in second-chance education
item.description: This article examines four life-histories from students who recently completed second-chance education at a Swedish folk high school, having previously left upper secondary school without full qualifications – an experience often associated with academic failure. item.title: The disorienting dilemma versus the event
item.description: We live in appalling times, in which it is almost impossible to remain hopeful; for radical adult educators, it is difficult to know what we should do in response. In this article, I draw on two theorists for possible inspiration. Jack Mezirow’s perspective transformation theory is one of the most widely used of all adult learning theories, but also continues to be critiqued as a theory of social change. item.title: Dynamics of motivation of older adults in training programmes
item.description: While educational programmes for older adults are critical for active ageing, their effectiveness depends on deeply understanding participation drivers beyond simplistic lists of motives. This systematic review synthesises evidence on motivations and barriers, reconceptualising motivation as a dynamic process that evolves from initial impulse to sustained engagement. item.title: Empowerment and adult education
item.description: Empowerment, as a goal of adult education, seeks to support people to critically reflect on structural settings and to take constructive action towards social equality and social change. item.title: ‘... we scratch our heads; we look at each other... we come up with a solution and we have no idea who came up with the solution... probably all together...’
item.description: This paper investigates aspects of informal and non-formal learning that emerge through adults’ participation in collective actions and social movements. item.description: This article explores the social, educational, and participatory practices during the revolutionary period in Portugal (1974-1976), a historical moment marked by a combination of political rupture and grassroots mobilisation. item.title: Beyond anthropocentrism
item.description: This article argues for the urgent reorientation of Adult Learning and Education (ALE) from its dominant anthropocentric paradigm toward an ecocentric foundation. item.title: Smooth sailing or hidden struggles?
item.description: For over two decades, quality has been a central and widely debated issue in lifelong learning.
